title: DraftAttention: Fast Video Diffusion via Low-Resolution Attention Guidance
original_abstract: Diffusion transformer–based video generation models (DiTs) have recently attracted widespread attention for their excellent generation quality. However, their computational cost remains a major bottleneck—attention alone accounts for over 80% of total latency, and generating just 8 seconds of 720p video takes tens of minutes—posing serious challenges to practical application and scalability. To address this, we propose the DraftAttention, a training-free framework for the acceleration of video diffusion transformers with dynamic sparse attention on GPUs. We apply down-sampling to each feature map across frames in the compressed latent space, enabling a higher-level receptive field over the latent composed of hundreds of thousands of tokens. The low-resolution draft attention map, derived from draft query and key, exposes redundancy both spatially within each feature map and temporally across frames. We reorder the query, key, and value based on the draft attention map to guide the sparse attention computation in full resolution, and subsequently restore their original order after the attention computation. This reordering enables structured sparsity that aligns with hardware-optimized execution. Our theoretical analysis demonstrates that the low-resolution draft attention closely approximates the full attention, providing reliable guidance for constructing accurate sparse attention. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing sparse attention approaches in video generation quality and achieves up to 1.75× end-to-end speedup on GPUs.

gaps_and_limitations.gap: Fixed pooling kernel size (8×16) may not be optimal for all video content types and resolutions
gaps_and_limitations.description: The paper uses a static 8×16 pooling kernel which may not adapt well to different video characteristics like fast motion, static scenes, or varying resolutions
gaps_and_limitations.improvement: Introduce adaptive pooling mechanisms that adjust kernel size based on motion analysis and content characteristics
gaps_and_limitations.runtime_change: Baseline: [n, n, d] → Original: [r*n², d, d] → Improved: [r'*n², d, d] where r' < r due to better sparsity patterns

gaps_and_limitations.gap: First 25% of denoising steps still use full attention, missing optimization opportunities
gaps_and_limitations.description: The method retains full attention for initial denoising steps which could still benefit from intelligent sparsity
gaps_and_limitations.improvement: Implement progressive sparsity that gradually increases from 0% to target sparsity across denoising steps
gaps_and_limitations.runtime_change: Original: 0.25*[n², d, d] + 0.75*[r*n², d, d] → Improved: Σ(i=1 to T) [r_i*n², d, d] where r_i increases monotonically

gaps_and_limitations.gap: Average pooling may lose fine-grained details important for high-frequency features
gaps_and_limitations.description: Simple average pooling can blur important high-frequency details that might be crucial for video quality
gaps_and_limitations.improvement: Use learnable pooling operators or attention-based pooling that preserves important features
gaps_and_limitations.runtime_change: Original: [g², d, d] for draft attention → Improved: [g², d, d] + [g², k, d] for attention weights (minimal overhead)

gaps_and_limitations.gap: No adaptive mechanism for different video content types (e.g., static vs dynamic scenes)
gaps_and_limitations.description: The method applies uniform sparsity regardless of video content characteristics
gaps_and_limitations.improvement: Implement content-aware sparsity that adjusts based on temporal motion analysis and spatial complexity
gaps_and_limitations.runtime_change: Original: [r*n², d, d] → Improved: [r_c*n², d, d] where r_c varies per content type (r_static < r_dynamic)

gaps_and_limitations.gap: Limited to specific resolution requirements for optimal performance
gaps_and_limitations.description: Optimal performance requires latent sizes divisible by 8×16 kernel, limiting flexibility
gaps_and_limitations.improvement: Develop dynamic padding and cropping strategies that maintain efficiency across arbitrary resolutions
gaps_and_limitations.runtime_change: No change in asymptotic complexity, but reduces padding overhead from O(p*n) to O(p)

gaps_and_limitations.gap: Single sparsity pattern across all attention heads may not be optimal
gaps_and_limitations.description: Different attention heads may focus on different aspects (spatial vs temporal patterns)
gaps_and_limitations.improvement: Implement head-specific sparsity patterns based on learned head importance or specialization
gaps_and_limitations.runtime_change: Original: [r*n², d, d] → Improved: Σ(h=1 to H) [r_h*n², d/H, d/H] where Σr_h < H*r

innovative_points.point: Low-resolution draft attention for dynamic sparse patterns
innovative_points.description: Uses downsampled query and key to compute lightweight attention maps that guide full-resolution sparsity
innovative_points.runtime_improvement: Reduces from O(n²d) to O(g²d + rn²d) where g = n/128, achieving 1.75× speedup
innovative_points.novelty: First to apply draft attention concept to video diffusion transformers without training

innovative_points.description: Deterministic reordering aligns region-level sparsity with token-level computation for coalesced memory access
innovative_points.runtime_improvement: Eliminates scattered memory access overhead, achieving practical 1.75× GPU speedup vs theoretical
innovative_points.novelty: Novel token reordering that bridges coarse sparsity with fine-grained computation

innovative_points.description: Plug-and-play integration requiring no additional training or fine-tuning
innovative_points.runtime_improvement: Zero overhead from training, immediate deployment benefit
innovative_points.novelty: First training-free sparse attention method for video diffusion with theoretical guarantees

innovative_points.point: Theoretical error bounds for approximation quality
innovative_points.description: Provides formal bounds on approximation error: ∥S-S_draft∥_F ≤ δn and ∥S-S⊙M̃∥_F ≤ n(δ+t)√(1-r)
innovative_points.runtime_improvement: Enables aggressive sparsity (90%) while maintaining quality bounds
innovative_points.novelty: First theoretical analysis of draft attention approximation in video generation context

innovative_points.description: Groups 128 tokens per processing unit matching GPU block sizes for optimal execution
innovative_points.runtime_improvement: Enables efficient kernel fusion and reduces memory transactions
innovative_points.novelty: Alignment of sparsity patterns with hardware block sizes for video transformers

improved_adaptive.complexity: Σ(t=1 to T) [r_t*n², d, d] + [g_t², d, d]
improved_adaptive.where: r_t varies by content and timestep

communication_overhead.improved: O(log n) with better caching strategies

additional_improvements.name: Multi-resolution draft attention
additional_improvements.description: Use multiple draft resolutions and select optimal based on content analysis

additional_improvements.name: Learnable sparsity thresholds
additional_improvements.description: Replace fixed sparsity ratio r with learned thresholds per region

additional_improvements.name: Temporal consistency enforcement
additional_improvements.description: Add temporal smoothness constraints to prevent flickering
additional_improvements.runtime: [r*n², d, d] + [n_frames*k, d, d] for temporal regularization
